title: For those who feel like giving up learning English

lines.text: If you can fall in love with a person,
can you fall in love with English? Yes.
Let me prove it. Step one, the love
journal. Buy a book and use it to write
about things you love. They can be
little things, big things, anything. But
here's the secret. Don't just write it,
feel it. The most successful people in
the world all understood the secret
power of love and gratitude. From Oprah
Winfrey to Albert Einstein to Leonardo
da Vinci, Oprah said, "Be thankful for
what you have, you'll end up having
more. If you concentrate on what you
don't have, you will never have enough."
So go buy that book and take action
today. Step two, romanticize your
relationship with English. Like falling
for a person, you're falling for a
process. So how do you fall in love with
a boy or a girl? You don't just admire
them from a distance.
You spend time with them. You make them
coffee. You write to them. So why not do
the same for English? Here are three
things you can romanticize. One,
romanticize the effort. Just like when
you enter in a new relationship, you
feel passion. And so loving is
effortless. Channel that passion into
self-development. Remind yourself that
the effort you make today is building
more positive feelings, positive
thoughts, and positive experiences in
your life. Two, romanticize the sounds
of words, how they roll off your tongue.
Treat English pronunciation as a fun
game. You could sing your favorite
songs, read poetry
aloud, or even write your own
poems. Three, romanticize your notebook.
This links back to step one, writing
gratitude and giving love to yourself in
English. Each notebook you fill is a
trophy. Celebrate every page and every
word you scribble. I've spent years
filling up these notebooks, and
honestly, it healed me. Most of mine are
a complete mess, but there's progress in
that mess. There's perfection in the
imperfection. So go buy that notebook,
mess it up, make it pretty, do whatever
you want because it's
yours. Step three, laugh at yourself.
When I lived in France, I used to get
tense and scared of making mistakes, so
I hid in my room and played FIFA all
day. Sure, I got sick at FIFA, but my
French
mad. Why? Because I was scared. Scared
of sounding silly. Scared of the
awkwardness, scared of what other people
might think. But when I moved to Spain,
I had some experience under my belt. I
was older,
carefree, curious, and that's how I got
fluent fast. Because I'd learned one
thing, laugh at yourself. I still made
mistakes, but I learned to enjoy them.
No one really cares if you mess up. No
one remembers. Everyone is too busy
thinking about their own mistakes. So
relax. Be a baby trying to walk and
talk. Don't overthink it. Just do it.
